claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child, Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about one child, **Alex**.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some information about your circumstances.

**First question: How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 17 years old.

**Next question: Is Alex still in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Alex is 17 and not currently in full-time education or approved training.

**Next question: Are you a UK resident, and do you have responsibility for Alex (for example, are you their parent or guardian)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me. I'm their parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. You're a UK resident and Alex lives with you as their parent.

**Next question: Does Alex have any income of their own, such as from employment or other sources?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Alex is working full-time.

**Next question: Approximately how much does Alex earn per week from their employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact amount, but they work full-time hours - more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex works more than 24 hours per week.

**Next question: To your knowledge, does Alex receive any state benefits, such as Income Support, Jobseeker's Allowance, Employment and Support Allowance, or Pension Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Final question: Are you currently receiving Child Benefit, or have you previously claimed it for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving it - that's why I'm inquiring to see if I'm eligible to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key facts:
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex is not in full-time education or approved training
- You are a UK resident and Alex's parent living with you
- Alex works full-time (more than 24 hours per week)
- Alex does not receive state benefits
- You are not currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, children must be under 16, or under 19 if they are in full-time education or approved training. Since Alex is 17 and not in full-time education or approved training, they do not meet the age and education requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: Unfortunately, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

**Reason:** Child Benefit is payable for children who are under 16 years old, or under 19 if they are in full-time education or approved training. Since Alex is 17 years old and is not currently in full-time education or approved training, they do not qualify.

If Alex were to return to full-time education or approved training, you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for them (up until they turn 19). If that changes, you could reapply.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
